chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one in Ihram must not touch anything of the perfume, nor the basil (or aromatic herb), nor derive pleasure from it, nor from a pleasant wind. So whoever is tested by something of that, let him give in charity according to the measure of what he did, according to his capacity.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for using perfume while in Ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi specifies that the prohibition extends beyond mere application to include touching, smelling, and deriving pleasure from any scent, reflecting the strict purity of the pilgrim's state. The requirement to give charity proportional to the 'extent' of the indulgence highlights the Shia juristic principle of compensating for sensory enjoyment, linking physical restraint with spiritual accountability during Hajj.
